rules: HM Land Registry states that the National Polygon Dataset is the published dataset of HMLR Index Polygons for England and Wales.
On completion of a registered title, HMLR normally produces a title plan, a register and one or more index polygons.
An HMLR title plan records the general position of registered-title boundaries unless a boundary has been determined as exact.
An HMLR register and title plan share the same title-number identifier.
Every registered title has at least one HMLR index polygon.
Each HMLR index polygon has a unique Polygon ID called Poly_ID.
The relationship between a registered title and its index polygons is managed through the title number.
HMLR index polygons are mapped against Ordnance Survey MasterMap large-scale data.
An HMLR index polygon follows a MasterMap feature only where that feature relates to the ownership boundary.
HMLR notes that ownership boundaries do not always follow features mapped in MasterMap.
The National Polygon Dataset is a subset of the Land Register containing registered titles relating to land or property.
The National Polygon Dataset is closely linked to the Title Descriptor dataset.
The National Polygon Dataset is closely linked to the Title Number and UPRN Look Up dataset.
HMLR separated National Polygon, Title Descriptor and UPRN data so the datasets are smaller and easier to manage.
The title number is the cross-dataset identifier used to link National Polygon data to other HMLR data.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are a subset of the National Polygon Dataset.
HMLR describes INSPIRE polygon attributes as simpler than National Polygon attributes.
The National Polygon Shape field is mandatory.
The National Polygon Shape field must contain a single-area geometry.
The National Polygon Poly_ID field is mandatory and numeric.
Poly_ID is unique to a spatial object and is managed through dataset lifecycle rules.
The National Polygon Title_No field is mandatory and character typed.
The National Polygon INSERT field is a mandatory date.
The INSERT field records when the polygon was initially created on the index map.
The National Polygon UPDATE field is a mandatory date.
The UPDATE field records when all or part of the title was last updated.
The National Polygon Vers_No field is mandatory and numeric.
Vers_No records the version of the Poly_ID.
The National Polygon Rec_Status field is mandatory and character typed.
National Polygon Rec_Status A means Added.
National Polygon Rec_Status C means Changed.
National Polygon Rec_Status D means Deleted.
HMLR states that minor index-polygon discrepancies should be resolved where registrations are intended to adjoin.
HMLR states that genuine gaps can exist where registered titles are not intended to adjoin.
An HMLR index polygon can be the same size as the title-plan extent.
An HMLR index polygon can be larger than the title-plan extent.
An HMLR index polygon can be smaller than the title-plan extent.
HMLR states that index polygons must not be relied on to show the exact extent of registered titles.
HMLR says the National Polygon Dataset contains inconsistencies arising from former capture practices.
Historic HMLR index polygons were manually captured on Ordnance Survey county-series sheets.
Historic HMLR index polygons were manually captured on national-grid sheets.
Historic HMLR index polygons were maintained in parcels books.
HMLR completed conversion of about 19 million paper index polygons to vector polygons in February 2004.
The vectorised 2004 index polygons were mapped against Ordnance Survey Land-Line.
HMLR receives a daily change-only update of OS MasterMap for creation of new index polygons and title plans.
HMLR does not use the daily OS MasterMap change-only update to automatically review all existing registrations.
Existing index polygons are updated when there is appropriate activity on a title or an adjoining title requires change.
HMLR states that all its data including index polygons is captured to British National Grid.
The National Polygon Dataset is published and updated monthly.
National Polygon files are updated and available from the second working day of each month.
National Polygon subscribers receive a full dataset file.
National Polygon subscribers receive change-only update files.
National Polygon subscribers receive validation files.
National Polygon CSV files use commas as field separators.
National Polygon CSV files enclose all fields in double quotes.
Blank National Polygon CSV fields are represented by empty quoted strings.
National Polygon CSV dates use DD-MM-YYYY format.
National Polygon CSV files use UTF-8 encoding.
National Polygon CSV delivery removes line separation within fields.
The first row of a National Polygon CSV file contains column headings.
The National Polygon full extract is split into multiple files because each file has a 2GB limit.
National Polygon full-file names follow LR_POLY_FULL_<month>_<file-number>.
National Polygon change-only filenames follow LR_POLY_COU_<DD_MMM_YYYY>.
National Polygon validation filenames follow LR_POLY_VALI_<month>.
The Title Number/UPRN Look Up dataset covers registered properties in England and Wales where an address association containing a UPRN can be made.
In the Title Number/UPRN Look Up dataset, Title_No is mandatory and character typed.
In the Title Number/UPRN Look Up dataset, UPRN is mandatory and integer typed.
HMLR records property addresses when land or property is registered.
HMLR links registration addresses to Ordnance Survey AddressBase where possible.
HMLR may create its own address when an address cannot be found in its Land Registry Property Gazetteer.
HMLR may later match its created address and title number to a new AddressBase address.
A title number and UPRN can be linked only where HMLR can establish a relationship between the AddressBase address and the title.
HMLR says duplicate addresses can exist in LRPG when supplied information does not match the gazetteer address.
An AddressBase address can have a UPRN but no associated HMLR title number if it is not present in LRPG.
HMLR moved to the Land Registry Property Gazetteer in 2002.
HMLR moved from AddressPoint to AddressLayer2 in 2011.
HMLR moved from AddressLayer2 to AddressBase as its national address source in 2014.
HMLR takes an AddressBase change-only update every six weeks for LRPG matching and title associations.
Within a six-week maintenance cycle, published UPRN linkage data shows only the last change made.
The Title Descriptor dataset gives estate interest and class of title for registered estates and interests in England and Wales.
The Planning Data API exposes more than 100 planning and housing datasets for England through one interface.
A Planning Data coordinate query constructs a point from latitude and longitude.
A Planning Data coordinate query returns entities whose geometry intersects the supplied point.
The longitude parameter requires latitude to be supplied.
The latitude parameter requires longitude to be supplied.
A Planning Data coordinate query can contain multiple dataset parameters.
When multiple dataset parameters are supplied, Planning Data returns matches from any selected dataset.
Planning Data recommends UPRN searches as more precise than coordinates for registered properties.
The Planning Data q parameter can search by postcode.
The Planning Data q parameter can search by UPRN.
Planning Data entity results can include name.
Planning Data entity results can include dataset.
Planning Data entity results can include start-date.
Planning Data entity results can include WKT geometry.
Planning Data entity results can include WKT point geometry.
Planning Data warns that absence of results does not prove absence of planning constraints.
Planning Data warns that data coverage can vary by area.
Planning Data documents an all-local-planning-authorities example returning 337 LPAs with a limit of 500.
Planning Data can use geometry_entity to filter entities using the geometry of another entity.
Planning Data documents geometry_relation=within for finding brownfield land inside an LPA boundary.
Planning Data documents scheduled-monument as a dataset usable in property screening.
Planning Data documents site-of-special-scientific-interest as a dataset usable in property screening.
Planning Data documents ancient-woodland as a dataset usable in property screening.
Planning Data documents heritage-at-risk as a dataset usable in property screening.
Planning Data documents area-of-outstanding-natural-beauty as a dataset usable in property screening.
Listed-building entities can include a listed_building_grade attribute.
Planning Data states that the planning-application specification is still in development.
Planning Data states that local planning authorities are not currently required to share application data to the developing planning-application specification.
Planning Data supports filtering planning applications by start_date_year.
Planning Data supports filtering planning applications by start_date_month.
Planning Data supports filtering planning applications by start_date_day.
Planning Data start_date_match accepts since.
Planning Data raw geometry queries accept WKT polygons.
Planning Data WKT geometry coordinates should be supplied in WGS84 EPSG:4326.
Spaces in Planning Data WKT query strings must be percent encoded.
Planning Data geometry_relation supports intersects.
Planning Data uses offset to page through large result sets.
Planning Data recommends incrementing offset by the limit value for successive pages.
Planning Data responses can include a prebuilt next-page link.
Planning Data responses can include a prebuilt previous-page link.
Planning Data responses can include a prebuilt first-page link.
Planning Data responses can include a prebuilt last-page link.
The Planning Data portfolio-screening API has no batch endpoint.
Planning Data recommends one API request per property for API-based portfolio screening.
Planning Data recommends field filters to reduce portfolio-screening response payloads.
The documented Planning Data portfolio example requests name, dataset and reference fields.
The documented Planning Data portfolio example uses a limit of 50.
Planning Data recommends polite rate limiting between per-property requests.
For hundreds of properties or more, Planning Data recommends bulk dataset downloads.
For large portfolios, Planning Data recommends local spatial intersections against downloaded datasets.
Planning Data describes bulk downloads as providing a stable snapshot for large-portfolio processing.
Planning Data bulk downloads are available as CSV.
Planning Data bulk downloads are available as JSON.
Planning Data bulk downloads can be available as GeoJSON.
Planning Data bulk downloads can be available as Parquet.
Planning Data states that Parquet is well suited to large datasets.
Planning Data notes that bulk-download URL formats vary by dataset.
The Planning Data Search entity endpoint is GET /entity.{extension}.
The Search entity extension must be json, html or geojson.
The Search entity typology parameter accepts an array of strings.
The Search entity organisation_entity parameter accepts an array of integers.
The Search entity curie parameter accepts an array of strings.
The Search entity prefix parameter accepts an array of strings.
The Search entity reference parameter accepts an array of strings.
The Search entity geometry_reference parameter can use geometries of entities matching supplied references.
The Search entity geometry_curie parameter can use geometries of entities matching supplied CURIEs.
The Search entity field parameter selects fields to include in the response.
The Search entity exclude_field parameter selects fields to exclude from the response.
When both field and exclude_field are supplied, Planning Data states that field takes precedence.
Planning Data publishes an OpenAPI JSON description that can be used to generate a client library.
The Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m is a raster elevation model.
The DTM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The DTM 1m has 1 metre spatial resolution.
The DTM 1m is produced from the last or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
DTM production removes surface objects from the DSM.
DTM surface-object removal uses bespoke algorithms.
DTM surface-object removal also uses manual editing.
The Environment Agency produced the current DTM 1m composite in 2022.
The DTM 1m combines Time Stamped archive surveys with National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where DTM 1m coverage repeats, the newest and best-resolution source is selected.
Where DTM 1m source data is resampled, bilinear interpolation is used before merging.
The DTM 1m composite includes source surveys from 6 June 2000.
The DTM 1m composite includes source surveys through 2 April 2022.
The DTM 1m metadata index catalogues identify which source survey was used at a location.
The DTM 1m is downloadable as GeoTIFF rasters.
The DTM 1m is distributed in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
DTM 1m elevations are expressed in metres.
DTM 1m elevations are referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
The DTM 1m uses the OSTN15 transformation method.
Individual LIDAR surveys contributing to DTM 1m are documented with ±15cm vertical RMSE.
The DTM 1m is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
The DTM 1m update frequency is annual.
The DTM 1m coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The DTM 1m metadata identifier is 13787b9a-26a4-4775-8523-806d13af58fc.
The DTM 1m dataset record exposes a WMS service.
The DTM 1m dataset record exposes a WCS service.
The DTM 1m dataset record exposes a WMTS service.
The DTM 1m dataset record exposes an OGC API Features service.
The DTM 1m metadata creation date is 8 February 2023.
The DTM 1m metadata revision date is 15 December 2023.
The DTM 2m is a raster elevation model covering approximately 99 percent of England.
The DTM 2m has 2 metre spatial resolution.
The DTM 2m is produced from the last or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
The DTM 2m combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where DTM 2m coverage repeats, the newest and best-resolution source is selected.
DTM 2m uses bilinear interpolation when source data must be resampled.
The DTM 2m is delivered as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km OS National Grid tiles.
DTM 2m elevations are in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
DTM 2m uses OSTN15.
The DTM 2m metadata identifier is 09ea3b37-df3a-4e8b-ac69-fb0842227b04.
The DTM 2m record exposes WMS, WCS and WMTS services.
The DTM 2m record exposes an OGC API Features service.
The DSM 1m is a raster elevation model covering approximately 99 percent of England.
The DSM 1m has 1 metre spatial resolution.
The DSM 1m is produced from the last or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
The DSM 1m includes heights of vehicles as well as the terrain surface.
The DSM 1m includes heights of buildings as well as the terrain surface.
The DSM 1m includes heights of vegetation as well as the terrain surface.
The DSM 1m combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
The DSM 1m metadata identifier is 9ba4d5ac-d596-445a-9056-dae3ddec0178.
The DSM 1m record exposes WMS, WCS and WMTS services.
The DSM 1m record exposes an OGC API Features service.
The First Return DSM 2m is a raster elevation model covering approximately 99 percent of England.
The First Return DSM 2m has 2 metre spatial resolution.
The First Return DSM 2m uses the first or only laser return.
The First Return DSM 2m can include vehicles.
The First Return DSM 2m can include buildings.
The First Return DSM 2m can include vegetation.
The First Return DSM 2m source programme ran from 11 November 2016 through 5 May 2022.
The National LIDAR Programme divided England into approximately 300 survey blocks.
The First Return composite uses feathering along survey overlaps to reduce small elevation differences.
The First Return DSM 2m does not necessarily match the coverage of the last-return DSM composite.
The First Return DSM 2m is delivered as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km OS National Grid tiles.
The First Return DSM 2m metadata identifier is 54167602-36c8-4b2b-80ec-ebb6267b6b1e.
The First Return DSM 2m record exposes WMS, WCS and WMTS services.
The First Return DSM 2m record exposes an OGC API Features service.
The Environment Agency survey-index OGC Features service advertises an OpenAPI 3 machine-readable API definition.
The Environment Agency survey-index OGC Features service advertises a collections endpoint.
The Environment Agency survey-index OGC Features service advertises conformance information.
The survey-index OGC Features collections use EPSG:27700 as storage CRS.
The survey-index service exposes a LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents collection.
The LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents collection exposes a filename string field.
The LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents collection exposes a tilename string field.
The LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents collection exposes a polygon_id string field.
The LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents collection exposes a resolution numeric field.
The LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents collection exposes a year field.
The LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents collection exposes an od_dtm_fn string field.
The LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents collection exposes survey start-date and end-date timestamp fields.
The survey-index service exposes a LIDAR_Composite_1m_First_Return_DSM_2022_extents collection.
The survey-index service exposes a LIDAR_Composite_1m_Last_Return_DSM_2022_extents collection.
The survey-index service exposes a LIDAR_Composite_2m_DTM_2022_extents collection.
The survey-index service exposes a LIDAR_Composite_2m_First_Return_DSM_2022_extents collection.
The survey-index service exposes a LIDAR_Composite_2m_Last_Return_DSM_2022_extents collection.
The survey-index service exposes a LIDAR_DSM_Time_Stamped_Extents collection.
The survey-index service exposes a LIDAR_DTM_Time_Stamped_Extents collection.
OS Terrain 50 is an open height dataset for Great Britain.
OS Terrain 50 is a digital terrain model with protruding features such as buildings and trees removed from the bare-earth surface.
OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July.
OS Terrain 50 is published as both grid and contour data.
OS Terrain 50 grid and contour data are created from the same source data.
OS Terrain 50 grid and contour tile supplies use 10km by 10km tiles.
Terrain 50 tiles are identified by the National Grid reference of the south-west corner.
Terrain 50 grid data uses regular 50m post spacing.
Terrain 50 contour data uses standard 10m contour intervals.
Terrain 50 contour data includes mean high water boundaries.
Terrain 50 contour data includes mean low water boundaries.
Terrain 50 contour data includes spot heights.
Terrain 50 grid is available in ASCII format.
Terrain 50 grid is available in GML 3.2.1 Simple Features Profile level 0.
Terrain 50 contours are available in GML 3.2.1 Simple Features Profile level 0.
Terrain 50 contours are available in Esri Shapefile.
Terrain 50 contours are available in GeoPackage.
Terrain 50 contours are available as vector tiles in MBTiles.
Terrain 50 online download requires no registration.
The tiled Terrain 50 national supply contains 2,858 10km tiles.
The 2,858 Terrain 50 tiles are arranged into 55 folders.
Each Terrain 50 tiled folder represents a 100km National Grid square.
Terrain 50 GeoPackage supply is a single national flat file.
Terrain 50 vector-tile supply is a single national flat file.
A full national Terrain 50 grid-tile supply is approximately 157 MB compressed.
Terrain 50 tiled data is compressed with ZIP.
Terrain 50 ZIP supply is not encrypted.
Terrain 50 is maintained through an integrated three-to-five-year flying programme.
Terrain 50 source terrain is captured as a triangulated irregular network.
The source TIN is edited using mass points.
The source TIN is edited using breaklines.
The source TIN can also use automated photogrammetric techniques.
Ordnance Survey states that TIN triangles retain feature edges more accurately than a regular grid.
Terrain 50 grid data is interpolated from the source TIN.
Terrain 50 contour data is interpolated from the source TIN.
The Terrain 50 source model records bare-earth X and Y coordinates as Eastings and Northings in OSGB36.
The Terrain 50 source model records Z as height in metres relative to the datum for the area.
Most Terrain 50 areas use Ordnance Survey Newlyn Datum.
A small number of offshore islands use a local height datum.
Terrain 50 bare-earth modelling excludes buildings.
Terrain 50 bare-earth modelling excludes supported structures where an air gap exists.
Terrain 50 bare-earth modelling excludes vegetation.
Terrain 50 modelling includes ground-level obstructions such as dams when they form part of the terrain.
Terrain 50 modelling includes breakwaters when they are wide enough to affect positional accuracy.
Terrain 50 modelling includes groynes when they are wide enough to affect positional accuracy.
Terrain 50 modelling includes relevant bridge revetments and earthworks as terrain.
Terrain 50 vegetation such as hedgerows and trees is removed from the bare-earth surface.
Terrain 50 models the top of a vertical feature at the correct planimetric location.
Terrain 50 offsets the lowest point of a vertical feature so only one z value occurs at a location.
Terrain 50 explicitly models major road and rail communication routes.
Terrain 50 route modelling removes extraneous features such as road furniture and bridges.
Terrain 50 route modelling includes associated slopes and embankments.
Terrain 50 mineral-working and landfill modelling captures outer limits, shape and depth.
Temporary spoil heaps are removed from Terrain 50 terrain modelling.
Contained flat-water bodies greater than 0.7 hectares are explicitly modelled.
The height assigned to a modelled contained water body is the lowest height of surrounding data.
Modelled contained-water surfaces are flat.
Terrain 50 ASCII grid tiles contain 200 columns.
Terrain 50 ASCII grid tiles contain 200 rows.
Each Terrain 50 ASCII grid pixel is 50m by 50m.
Terrain 50 ASCII grid rows run west to east.
Successive Terrain 50 ASCII rows begin 50m south of the preceding row.
Terrain 50 grid height values are given to the nearest 0.1m.
Terrain 50 grid supply includes a per-tile metadata XML file.
Terrain 50 GML geometries use EPSG:27700 expressed as urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::27700.

Exact candidate HMLR INSPIRE IDs and native-BNG containment remain unresolved; no identity promotion is allowed.
Exact Planning Data coordinate responses for all three candidates remain blocked by execution URL safety.
Exact Planning Data responses for parcel references 52040420, 52213916 and 52213412 remain absent.
Environment Agency OGC Features catalogue and DTM extent schema are readable, but exact TQ2892 filtered survey feature has not been read back.
The official DTM 1m WCS GetCapabilities URL is known, but this client cannot parse the application/xml response and no candidate GetCoverage GeoTIFF bytes or numeric elevations are captured.
Official OS Terrain 50 technical documentation is readable, but official Downloads API product JSON for Terrain50 is still not read back.
Actual Terrain50 TQ29 grid bytes, checksum and row149 col173/174 numeric values remain absent.
F-host guarded recovery, HD2 operator preflight 015, HD1 revision14 output 016, integrity readback 025 and identity-provenance runtime remain absent; second runner is forbidden.
